subject: Contract question: export controls + runtime access in DPA (Northbridge)
messages:

Cc: contracts@northbridge-systems.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed DPA terms — runtime export controls

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking a look at our DPA draft. We reviewed the redlines and have two outstanding asks before procurement can move forward:

1) Section 4.3 (Data Exports): We need explicit language that Redwood will not export raw request/response logs or KV cache content outside of the EU/US environment without prior written consent from Northbridge. This is a hard requirement for our compliance team.

2) Section 7.2 (Subprocessors): We require a list of subprocessors that will have runtime access to customer data (including telemetry collectors), and a quarterly disclosure schedule.

We've attached our redlined DPA (DPA_Northbridge_v2_redlined.pdf). Can you confirm whether these are acceptable or if they trigger product/security exceptions? Procurement is aiming to have signed docs by 28 Jul.

If helpful, happy to hop on a short call with engineering/security.

Thanks,
Laura Chen

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed DPA terms — runtime export controls

Short technical read:
- KV cache: Our runtime keeps KV cache in GPU/ephemeral host memory and it is not persisted to blob storage by default. There is no supported feature that exports KV cache off-cluster.
- Request/response logs: We collect telemetry and structured logs; some teams may ship aggregated telemetry to third-party analytics (opt-in for customers). Raw request/response logs are treated as sensitive and we only persist them for short retention windows (customer-configurable).

Implications for the contract asks:
- The "no export of raw KV cache" statement is technically accurate with current product behavior; however, to make it an explicit contractual guarantee we should clarify the terms that define "export" (e.g., persistent storage, backup, or transfer to third-party).
- If Northbridge expects us to add a technical control (e.g., automated blocking of any admin-initiated export), that would require a small engineering change and ~2 weeks of work to add a config flag + audit log hook.

Suggested language (technical):
"Redwood will not persist or transfer in raw form any per-request KV cache or runtime-only model working state to external third parties, except as required for debugging with prior written consent. 'Persist' excludes ephemeral in-memory caching used for inference."

I attached a short note explaining KV cache behavior (tech_note_kv_cache_behavior.txt). If legal wants stronger wording we should coordinate on definitions.

— Aditya
attachments: tech_note_kv_cache_behavior.txt (text, 4KB)

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed DPA terms — runtime export controls

Thanks, team — good notes. My take and proposed next steps:

1) Product position: We can accept a no-export clause for KV cache and raw request/response data with the clarifying definitions Aditya suggested. That avoids committing to building new enforcement controls immediately.

2) Subprocessor disclosure: we already maintain a living list of subprocessors and can offer quarterly disclosures. Security should confirm whether telemetry collectors fall under "runtime access" — my recommendation is to treat telemetry as a disclosed subprocessor but note that telemetry collects aggregated signals only; raw traces are not included in that disclosure by default.

3) Contract language: I've drafted a short acceptance template that combines the technical language and a commercial note about the disclosure cadence. See attached acceptance_template.txt. Recommended paragraph to send external:

"Redwood confirms that it will not persist or transfer raw KV cache or raw request/response data to third parties outside the environments agreed in the DPA, except with prior written consent for debugging. Redwood will provide a quarterly list of subprocessors with runtime access, and will note any telemetry processors with the scope of data they may receive (aggregated metrics only)."

4) Next steps: send Laura the suggested text and offer a 30-minute sync with Aditya and Markus if Northbridge wants technical assurances. If they push back on definitions, loop Legal (Markus can I have you do a quick check and sign off on the proposed clause?)

I'll prepare a one-email response to external with the proposed language unless you object.

— Evelyn Hart
VP, Product | Redwood Inference
